mission: First port of the SDLC wizard pattern to OpenCode CLI. Phase A scope: hooks, skills, AGENTS.md, install.sh. The bash hooks are ported verbatim from BaseInfinity/claude-sdlc-wizard (the parent) and BaseInfinity/codex-sdlc-wizard (the closest sibling). The novel/risky surface is the JS plugin shim at .opencode/plugins/sdlc-wizard.js — OpenCode does NOT have a Claude-style declarative hook config, so plugins subscribe to events (session.created, tool.execute.before, experimental.session.compacting) and shell out to the bash hooks. AGENTS.md replaces the per-prompt SDLC BASELINE since OpenCode has no UserPromptSubmit analog.
success: Reviewer reads the plugin shim against OpenCode plugin docs (https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/) and confirms the event names + handler signatures match. Verifies the install.sh is non-destructive on existing opencode.json and existing customized AGENTS.md. Verifies skill paths match OpenCode discovery rules (https://opencode.ai/docs/skills/). Confirms exit-code-2 block contract for the compact event is wired correctly.
failure: Superficial review will miss: (a) plugin event names being slightly off — e.g., the actual OpenCode API uses `tool.execute.before` but with a different argument shape than {tool, args}, so our destructure breaks silently; (b) the plugin's bash invocation may be on a slow path because `child_process.execFile` blocks the OpenCode event loop while bash runs (each hook ~10-50ms — could matter in tight tool-execute loops); (c) the AGENTS.md → SDLC BASELINE move loses the per-prompt cadence and we don't have a fallback nudge mechanism; (d) install.sh's wizard-stamp file is not yet consumed by anything — drift detection isn't implemented; (e) opencode.json plugin registration: do plugins at .opencode/plugins/ auto-load, or does the user need to add the plugin to opencode.json's `plugin` array?
verification_checklist: (a) Plugin event names match OpenCode plugin docs. Specifically: `session.created`, `tool.execute.before`, `experimental.session.compacting`. Verify each handler signature destructures the right argument shape. Cross-check with https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/.

(b) Plugin entry point matches OpenCode calling convention. Should export an async function that takes `{ project, client, $, directory, worktree }` and returns an object whose keys are event names. Verify .opencode/plugins/sdlc-wizard.js:60-69.

(c) Plugin's exit-code-2 block contract on `experimental.session.compacting`. Throwing inside the handler should propagate as a block. Verify .opencode/plugins/sdlc-wizard.js:91-99 — does throwing actually block in OpenCode's plugin runtime?

(d) Skill paths resolve under OpenCode discovery rules: `.opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (project-local). Per https://opencode.ai/docs/skills/, OpenCode walks up from cwd to git worktree root. Confirm install.sh installs to the right path.

(e) AGENTS.md auto-loads at session start (https://opencode.ai/docs/rules/). Verify our AGENTS.md format is plain markdown with no required frontmatter; verify it's at repo root (not under .opencode/).

(f) install.sh idempotency: re-running on already-installed target is a no-op. Verify by running `bash install.sh --target-dir TMP && bash install.sh --target-dir TMP` and confirming second run reports all MATCH, zero INSTALLED. (Test 2 in tests/test-install.sh does this.)

(g) install.sh non-destructive: existing opencode.json is untouched (test 6), existing customized AGENTS.md is preserved (test 3, kept-customized). Verify the classify() function correctly distinguishes MATCH/CUSTOMIZED/MISSING.
(h) Hook scripts are byte-identical between top-level hooks/ and .opencode/hooks/ (no drift). Verify cmp -s passes for all 5 hooks (test_bundle's drift guard).
(i) The 4 skills installed at .opencode/skills/<n>/SKILL.md have the right frontmatter for OpenCode discovery (lowercase-alphanumeric-with-hyphens name; required `name` and `description` fields).
(j) Plugin uses `node:child_process` (portable), NOT bun-only `$` — confirm the plugin runs under plain Node too. Verify import line.
(k) Source-glob regex (TDD-pretool filter) covers common source extensions and excludes test/spec/fixtures paths. test-plugin-shim.sh::SOURCE_GLOB_RE check is the proof.
(l) No leak of Claude-specific event names as plugin handler keys (anti-regression for the OpenCode adaptation). test-bundle-integrity.sh::plugin-leak guards prove this.
(m) Sibling-family cross-references in AGENTS.md and README.md list all 4 siblings (claude-sdlc-wizard, codex-sdlc-wizard, claude-gdlc-wizard, opencode-sdlc-wizard).
(n) HANDOFF.md research checklist items are all marked [x] with discovered facts (not still [ ] open questions).

(o) ~/xdlc skill-triple pattern compliance: setup/update/feedback skills have distinct trust-and-mutation footprints per docs/skill-triple-pattern.md. Verify the 3 skills don't conflate scopes (setup creates body, update touches metadata only, feedback writes only to append-only log).
review_instructions: You are an independent code reviewer performing a certification audit on the FIRST RELEASE of a port. The bash hooks themselves are unchanged from two earlier siblings (claude-sdlc-wizard and codex-sdlc-wizard) — DO NOT re-review them. Focus your scrutiny on the OpenCode-specific adapter surface: the JS plugin shim, the install.sh, and the architectural decisions documented in HANDOFF.md and CHANGELOG.md. Specifically verify the plugin's event-handler signatures against OpenCode's actual plugin docs (https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/). The bootstrap session researched the events from public docs but did NOT run the wizard end-to-end against a live OpenCode install. Be strict: if the plugin's destructured event payload (e.g., `{ tool, args }` for `tool.execute.before`) doesn't match OpenCode's actual API, that's a P0 — silent runtime failure. Use ALL THREE sibling repos as reference: BaseInfinity/claude-sdlc-wizard (parent), BaseInfinity/codex-sdlc-wizard (closest port pattern), and ~/xdlc (umbrella patterns including skill-triple-pattern.md). End with: score (1-10), CERTIFIED or NOT CERTIFIED.
